title: Human-attention flag
description: Schema for .scrum/attention.json. Records whether Claude is currently blocked on the human, so an external UI (the Mac app) can raise a banner without reading transcripts. Written by the hook process hooks/notification-attention.sh: a Notification event sets pending:true, a UserPromptSubmit event clears it to pending:false. Consumers treat a missing file, an unparseable file, and pending != true as identical: nothing is waiting. Writers: hooks/notification-attention.sh only (no .scrum/scripts/*.sh wrapper — hook hot-path).

pending.description: True while Claude is waiting on the human. Cleared to false on the next UserPromptSubmit.

type.description: Which kind of wait this is, mirroring the Notification payload's notification_type. 'permission_prompt' = an unanswered tool-permission dialog; 'idle_prompt' = the turn ended and no prompt followed within the harness idle window. An unknown/absent notification_type is normalized to 'idle_prompt' by the writer. Required while pending is true.

message.description: Banner text. For idle_prompt this is the turn's last_assistant_message recovered from attention-context.json when the prompt_id matches, otherwise the Notification payload's own (generic) message. Truncated by the writer to 200 codepoints plus an ellipsis. Required while pending is true.

agent.description: Teammate display name resolved from .scrum/session-map.json by session id (e.g. 'dev-001-s1'). Omitted entirely when the session is unmapped — the common case for the Scrum Master's own session.

updated_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of this write (both the set and the clear path refresh it).
